content.title: 15 Best Things to Do in Fujian: Top 15 Fujian Attractions 2026
content.text: Fujian, nestled along the southeastern coastline of China, is a wonderful province with pleasant weather that is suitable to be visited all year round. Full of precious UNESCO world heritages, amazing mountains and streams, sacred temples, mottled lanes and alleys, well-kept ancient dwellings, golden beaches, unbeatable coastal views, etc., Fujian Province is nothing short of magnificent! Its most popular tourist destinations include Xiamen, Fujian Tulou, Wuyi Mountain, Quanzhou, Fuzhou, Xiapu, etc. Below, we've listed 15 Best Things to Do in Fujian, all centered in these destinations, and you can check them to plan a better 2026 Fujian Tour in China! Fujian Tourist Attractions Map (Click to enlarge) No.1 Pay a Visit to Fujian Tulou for Gigantic and Unique Hakka Dwellings Yongding Tulou Nanjing Tulou Tulu, also called earthen buildings, are the traditional dwellings in gigantic sizes and round, square, oval, or other shapes, with the largest one able to hold 800 members to live at once. The main structural walls of the buildings are made of mud, hence the name. Tulou were all built for defensive use at the beginning, but now they serve as homes of locals and attractions for visitors heading to explore the history, unique architectural design, and Hakka culture of this region. In 2008, Fujian Tulou, including all the Tulou buildings at 3 major areas in Fujian, was listed as a cluster of World Cultural Heritage Sites. The 3 major areas include Nanjing Tulou, Yongding Tulou and Hua'an Dadi Tulou. Nanjing Tulou (南靖土楼), which dates back to the mid-Yuan Dynasty (1308-1338 CE), is the most popular Tulou region of Fujian Tulou. Its Tianluokeng Tulou Cluster, which leaves a great impression on visitors for the lovely distribution of its 5 Tulou that just like Four Dishes and One Soup on a Chinese dining table, is usually a must-visit for all Tulou lovers. Nanjing Tulou also offers many other great Tulou at its Yunshuiyao Scenic Area, Hekeng Tulou Cluster, Taxia Village, etc. Yongding Tulou (永定土楼), dating back to 766-779 CE, is another important member of Fujian Tulou. Compared with Nanjing Tulou, Yongding Tulou is a little bit further from Xiamen, the best gateway to visit Fujian Tulou. However, this is seldom a big problem for visitors heading there if you have the help of a convenient and efficient private car service with a local driver included. Yongding Tulou is also composed of several parts, including Hongkeng Tulou Cluster, Gaobei Tulou Cluster, Chuxi Tulou Cluster, and Nanxi Tulou Cluster. Hua'an Dadi Tulou (华安大地土楼) is often not that famous compared with Nanjing Tulou and Yongding Tulou, because it is relatively far and not that impressive. However, there are still three earthen buildings that have been listed in the World Heritage Site List, including Eryi Building, Nanyang Building, and Dongyang Building. Type: Cultural Site, UNESCO World Cultural Heritage Site, Ancient Dwellings, Historical Relics Tickets: from CNY 50 per person Best Time to Visit: all year around Recommended Trip Length: 1~3 days Nanjing Tulou Location: Nanjing County, Zhangzhou City, Fujian, China (福建省漳州市南靖县) Yongding Tulou Location: Yongding District, Longyan City, Fujian, China (福建省龙岩市永定区) No.2 Soak Up the Sun and Browse International Architectures at Gulangyu Island in Xiamen Gulangyu Island Gulangyu Island Gulangyu Island (鼓浪屿) is situated at the southern part of Xiamen, Fujian. With reputations like "A Garden on the Sea", "Exhibition of World's Architecture" and "The Hometown of Music", Gulangyu Island is a popular tourist island with splendid coastal sceneries, old international architectures, and numerous interesting museums that are perfect for vacation. This relatively compact island boasts over 1,000 historical buildings and countless lanes, alleys, gardens, and beaches. Highlights include Sunlight Rock, Shuzhuang Garden, Piano Museum, Haoyue Garden, Organ Museum, and so on. To get to Gulangyu Island, visitors are required to catch a ferry at one of the three ports in Xiamen, including Dongdu Ferry Terminal, Xiamen Lundu Port, and Songyu Port. During the day, Dongdu Ferry Terminal is the most popular choice, while Lundu Port is more popular at night, because it is the only port with a night ship available. On the Gulangyu Island Side, there are also two ports for you to choose from, including Sanqiutian Port and Neicuoao Port. Sanqiutian Port has both day ferries and night ferries, while Neicuoao Port only provides ferry service to/from Dongdu Feryy Terminal during the day. Type: Island, Natural Scenery, Architecture Tickets: free Best Time to Visit: all year around Recommended Trip Length: half day or one day Location: Siming District, Xiamen, Fujian, China (福建省厦门市思明区) No.3 Indulge in Stunning Landscape and Charming Taoist, Buddhist, Confucian Culture at Wuyi Mountain Nine Bends Stream Bamboo Rafting Wuyi Mountain View from Top Wuyi Mountain Scenic Resort (武夷山风景名胜区), or called Wuyi Mountain or Wuyishan for short, is located in Wuyishan City of Nanping City in the northern part of Fujian Province. Entitled as a World Natural and Cultural Heritage Site by UNESCO, Wuyi Mountain has no shortage of awe-inspiring wonders, natural, historic, and cultural, each more picture-perfect than the next. The most attractive experience in Wuyi Mountain is the amazing bamboo rafting through Nine Bends Stream, with picturesque karst landscape slowly moving by and a gentle breeze blowing through your face. The moment you get off the bamboo raft, you will be rewarded with Wuyi Palace, the oldest Taoist temple of the whole Wuyi Mountain Scenic Resort that used to be the place where the emperors offered sacrifices to the gods. Wuyi Mountain is also a famous mountain of three religions—Confucianism, Buddhism and Taoism—rare to see in other places in China. Stroll around Wuyi Mountain, and you will find many well-preserved old architectures and a museum. Not far from the palace is a food street with various kinds of snacks for you to try. Wuyi Mountain is also a paradise for hiking and trekking. Tianyou Peak, also named Heavenly Peak, offers an excellent view of the surrounding landscape and is the most popular for hiking. In addition to Tianyou Peak, there are also Tiger Roaring Peak, Great King Peak, etc. The most exquisite trekking trail is the Yangu Huaxiang Hiking Trail from Dahongpao Scenic Area to Water Curtain Cave. Dahongpao Scenic Area is the place where one of China's greatest teas—Da Hong Pao Tea—grows. After night falls, a large-scale live performance named Impression Da Hong Pao is about to start, which is really a visual and audio enjoyment. Impression Dah Hong Pao is held in the open air in front of Mount Wuyi, with the real landscape of Wuyishan decorated with multicolored lights as the backdrop. Type: Mountains, Natural Site, UNESCO Cultural and Natural Site, Tea Plantation Tickets: from CNY 140 per person Best Time to Visit: spring, summer and early autumn Recommended Trip Length: 2~3 days Location: Wuyishan City, Nanping City, Fujian, China (福建省南平市武夷山市) No.4 Gain Insight into the Maritime Silk Road Glory of Quanzhou Kaiyuan Temple Ancient Ships Displayed at Quanzhou Maritime Museum Quanzhou, the UNESCO-recognized starting point of the Maritime Silk Road in the Song and Yuan dynasties, is a historic and cultural gem where diverse cultures converge. It weaves together local Minnan (South Fujian) traditions, influences from China's central plains, and legacies of religions like Buddhism, Hinduism, Islam, and Christianity. This city encompasses 22 representative world heritage sites and numerous excellent historic spots. They include the 1,300-year-old Kaiyuan Temple (开元寺), the Maritime Silk Road witness with famous East and West Towers; Quanzhou Maritime Museum, the first maritime museum in China, housing remarkable 9,365 maritime artifacts; Qingjing Mosque (清净寺), one of the oldest Islamic temples in China; Tianhou Temple (天后宫), the earliest and most prestigious temple to worship Mazu globally; Luoyang Bridge (洛阳桥), one of the country's four famous ancient bridges; bustling Quanzhou West Street (泉州西街) and Zhongshan Road (中山路) with various architectural elements of cultural fusion... Most of them are located within or near the Quanzhou old town. In the suburbs, the Xunpu Village (蟳埔村), said to be where Arab descendants live, stands out for its intangible heritage—Xunpu women's custom, and its unique oyster shell dwellings. To walk through Quanzhou is to step into the Maritime Silk Road's golden era, where every corner tells a story of ancient trade and cultural exchange. Type: Religious & Cultural Site, UNESCO World Cultural Heritage Sites Tickets: free Best Time to Visit: all year around Recommended Trip Length: 2~3 days Old Town Location: Licheng District, Quanzhou City, Fujian, China (福建省泉州市鲤城区) Xunpu Village Location: Fengze District, Quanzhou City, Fujian, China (福建省泉州市丰泽区) No.5 Trace China's Modern History at Sanfang Qixiang in Fuzhou Sanfang Qixiang Panorama of Sanfang Qixiang Sanfang Qixiang (三坊七巷) is a busy historical block in the city center of Fuzhou. Its name, Sanfang, literally means "three lanes," and Qixiang means "seven alleys" in English. Therefore, Sanfang Qixiang is also known as Three Lanes and Seven Alleys. As its name implies, Sanfang Qixiang is composed of three mottled lanes and seven historical alleys. In between those lanes and alleys are over 270 well-preserved old dwellings, some of which are the homes of many celebrities in China's modern history. Sanfang Qixiang enjoys many reputations, like "Top 10 Famous Historical and Cultural Streets in China", "The Beverly Hills of Imperial China", "Living Fossils of China's Urban Lane System", and "Museum of Chinese Architecture of Ming and Qing Dynasties". A tour getting close to Sanfang Qixiang is said to somewhat step back to China's modern history. As a famous saying goes, "One Sanfang Qixiang equals half of China's modern history," which is perfect evidence of its significant role in history. Aside from its old dwellings, nowadays Sanfang Qixiang is also a busy tourist site for foodies and shoppers. Rows of small shops, restaurants, and other entertainments are open on the two sides of the lanes and alleys. Whether you are looking for something to eat or some handicrafts and souvenirs to buy, Sanfang Qixiang will give you what you want. Most of the shops won't be closed until midnight. Besides Sanfang Qixiang, travelers to Fuzhou can also visit the important Museum of Foochow Arsenal 1866, Luoxing Tower, Xichan Temple, Lin Zexu Memorial Hall. Type: Historic Block, Ancient Lanes and Alleys, Ancient Dwellings Tickets: free Best Time to Visit: all year around Recommended Trip Length: half a day or one day Location: Gulou District, Fuzhou, Fujian, China (福建省福州市鼓楼区) No.6 Uncover Millennia-Old Buddhist Relics and Xiamen Panoramas at South Putuo Temple Panorama of South Putuo Temple South Putuo Temple Buddhist Architecture South Putuo Temple (南普陀寺), nestled against Wulao Peak in the southeast of Xiamen, is one of Fujian's most thriving Buddhist temples and one of the eight scenic spots in Xiamen. It enshrines Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva and is located south of Putuo (Potalaka) Mountain at its south, which is where it gets its name. First founded in the Tang Dynasty (618-907 AD), the temple underwent a major renovation in 1662-1722 CE of the Qing Dynasty. Facing south, the temple is built against the mountain and overlooks the sea, with structures rising tier by tier along the terrain. Grand and solemn, its main buildings align with the central axis, featuring exquisite ancient palace-style architecture — double-eaved roofs with upturned ridges, apricot-yellow glazed tiles, and vibrant carvings. Key structures include the Mahavira Hall, Heavenly King Hall, Scripture Repository, etc., and a releasing pond in front of the temple. The temple's vegetarian cuisine is another highlight, and its vegetarian pastries are a well-known Xiamen specialty. After exploring its major architecture, visitors can hike up Wulao Peak via trails to have a panorama of Xiamen City, covering landmarks like Xiamen University, Gulangyu Island, the Twin Towers, and Xiamen Botanic Garden. Type: Religious Site, Ancient Architecture Tickets: free Best Time to Visit: all year around Recommended Trip Length: 1~3 hours Location: No. 515 Siming South Road, Siming District, Xiamen, Fujian, China (福建省厦门市思明区思明南路515号) No.7 Admire Chinese-Western Overseas Chinese Architecture in Xiamen's Jimei School Village Jimei School Village Jiageng Park at Jimei School Village Jimei School Village is the collective name for various schools and cultural institutions on Jimei Peninsula in Xiamen. Founded in 1913 by renowned patriotic overseas Chinese leader Chen Jiageng, it covers over 2 million square meters, with a comprehensive education system from preschool to doctoral level. There are also public amenities like Funan Auditorium, the Dragon Boat Pool, a park, and a sailing club—integrating education with daily and recreational needs. Every year, grand dragon boat races are held at the Dragon Boat Pool during the Dragon Boat Festival. Its structures blend Chinese and Western architectural styles: from grand school buildings to delicate pavilions, all adorned with glazed-tile roofs, dragon-and-phoenix ridges, and carved beams, forming a unique scenic sight. To the southeast lies Ao Garden, a turtle-shaped islet, where you can discover over 650 blue stone carvings—masterpieces of Minnan stone culture. The village also houses Chen Jiageng's Former Residence and a museum showcasing his life story, commemorating his contributions. Here, the strong atmosphere of Jiageng Culture and Jiageng Spirit—rooted in patriotism, dedication to education, self-discipline, lifelong social service, and frugal public devotion—has inspired countless people and attracted more visitors eager to learn about his legacy. Type: Chinese-Western Architecture, Natural and cultural Sightseeing Tickets: free Best Time to Visit: all year around Recommended Trip Length: half a day or one day Location: No. 183 Yinjiang Road, Jimei Street, Jimei District, Xiamen, Fujian, China (福建省厦门市集美区集美街道银江路183号) No.8 Capture China's Most Beautiful Coastline at Xiapu Mudflat Xiapu Mudflat (霞浦滩涂), a beautiful place in Xiapu County, Ningde City, Fujian, is very famous among photographers. It is praised as one of the "Top 10 Domestic Photography Bases" by photography enthusiasts. This stunning region is a masterpiece co-created by the wind, the sun, the sea, the earth, the beach, the surrounding mountains, and also the local "sea gypsies". With the rotation of the earth and the movement of the sun and wind, the tides rise and fall. The wet mudflats are sparkling in a mixed ever-changing color, like pink, golden, blue, white, gray, etc. The surrounding mountains and rows or rings of bamboo poles, fish nets, and stone columns inset by the local fishermen add more mysterious shadows and a sense of layers to the scenery. Every corner and every second in Xiapu Mudflat are just so amazing that they will stop your steps to leave and make you want to return over and over again! There is a series of places to create beautiful pictures in Xiapu Mudflat, including Beiqi Village, Gulingxia Village, Shatangli Village, Shajiang Village, Hanjiang Village, etc. Type: Natural Site Tickets: free Best Time to Visit: all year around Recommended Trip Length: 1~3 days Location: Xiapu County, Ningde City, Fujian, China (福建省宁德市霞浦县) No. 9 Indulge in Diverse Tea Scents and Esteemed Tea Culture of Fujian Fujian is like a "tea aroma museum", where every inch of land is steeped in the rich heritage of a thousand-year tea history. Wuyi Rock Tea of Wuyi Mountain, especially Dahongpao tea (大红袍), boasts a crispo, lingering rock rhyme, with the fragrance of rocks and flowers slowly unfolding on your taste buds; Anxi Tieaguanyin (安溪铁观音) in Quanzhou, one of ten most famous tea in China, whether as fresh and elegant as orchids or as mellow as honey, showcases the versatile charm of oolong tea through its varied aromas; Fuding White Tea has a sweet, mild downy scent, as if infused with the clear, fresh essence of high-mountain clouds and mist; and Fuzhou Jasmine Tea blends the soft fragrance of jasmine with tea aroma, delivering the exquisite delight of "infusing jasmine to achieve the supreme taste" straight to your heart. Explore Fujian's mountain-terraced tea plantations, where lush green views abound, and experience to pick fresh tea leaves, observe the traditional tea-making process. Then slow down, settle at a mountainside tea table, or find a place by the sea in Fujian, brew a pot of fine tea, let the varied aromas wrap around you, and soak in the one-of-a-kind tea charm that is uniquely Fujian's. Type: Culture, Tea Plantation Tickets: Tea Price Best Time to Visit: April to October Recommended Trip Length: 2 hours to half a day Wuyi Rock Tea Location: Wuyishan City, Nanping City, Fujian, China (福建省南平市武夷山市) Anxi Tieguanyin Location: Anxi County, Quanzhou City, Fujian, China (福建省泉州市安溪县) No.10 Dive into Fujian's Rich Intangible Cultural Heritages in Quanzhou Quanzhou Intangible Culture Heritage Museum Quanzhou Marionette Theater Fujian boasts a wealth of intangible cultural heritage, and Quanzhou stands out as a must-visit destination for experiencing these treasures. The Quanzhou Intangible Culture Heritage Museum is unmissable. It is China's largest museum dedicated to intangible cultural heritage, showcasing nearly 50 ICH items and over 650 exhibits. It displays traditional artworks like stone and wood carvings, flower lanterns;local customs such as Xunpu Women's Hair Adornment Tradition, Wuzu Boxing; traditional operas like Marionette Opera, Gaojia Opera; and time-honored craftsmanship such as such as Dehua Porcelain Firing Technique, Anxi Oolong Tea-Making Technique..., as well as hosts performances by inheritors. Another highlight is the Quanzhou Marionette Theater. Quanzhou's marionette art is a globally acclaimed masterpiece, and this theater is the best place to enjoy the show, for the troupe here has graced major home and international media and won numerous awards. Zhongshan Road in Quanzhou is also a good spot. This vibrant thoroughfare hosts live performances including Nanyin music, Houding Gongpo dance, South Shaolin martial arts..., perfect for feeling the city's cultural energy. Type: Cultural Site, Intangible Cultural Heritage Tickets: CNY 20-80 for Quanzhou Marionette Theater; free for others Best Time to Visit: all year around Recommended Trip Length: 1~3 hours Museum Location: No. 648, Donghu Street, Fengze District, Quanzhou City, Fujian, China (福建省泉州市丰泽区东湖街648号) Theater Location: No. 355, Quanshan Road, Fengze District, Quanzhou City, Fujian, China (福建省泉州市丰泽区泉山路355号) Zhongshan Road Location: Zhongshan Middle Road, Licheng District, Quanzhou City, Fujian, China (福建省泉州市鲤城区中山中路) No.11 Immerse Yourself in Brilliant Impression Da Hong Pao in Wuyi Mountain Impression Da Hong Pao (印象大红袍) is a spectacular landscape-based live performance co-created by renowned Chinese directors Zhang Yimou, Wang Chaoge, and Fan Yue. It takes the Wuyi Mountain—the UNESCO World Natural and Cultural Heritage Site—as its outdoor stage, and holds at the world's first "circular landscape theater" with a total visual stage length of 12,000 meters. Cleverly integrating Wuyi's natural scenery, the profound 600-year heritage of Wuyi Rock Tea culture, and local folk traditions into one show, it has become a must-see for all visitors to Wuyi Mountain. The performance weaves in Wuyi's classic love tale of "King Peak & Jade Maiden Peak", and combines drama, Tang Dynasty dances, and dynamic lighting, turning tea into a cultural symbol of millennia of human sentiment. As night falls, lights glide across the rock faces and mist drifts through the valleys; the audience feels less like they are "watching a show" and more like they have stepped into a poetic painting of Wuyi's scenery. Adding to its appeal is its world's first 360-degree rotating audience platform, which completes a full rotation slowly in just 5 minutes. Audiences can easily follow the story from all angles. Type: Performance, Cultural Highlight Tickets: CNY 208 Best Time to Visit: all year around Length of Time: about 70 mins Location: No. 16, Huandao South Road, Sangu Resort, Wuyishan City, Nanping City, Fujian, China (福建省南平市武夷山市三姑度假区环岛南路 16 号) No.12 Hit a Restaurant There to Treat Yourself with Delicious Min Cuisine and Seafood Buddha Jumps over the Wall Gulangyu Island Snacks Foodies? You should never forget to treat yourself to the delicious Min Cuisine (Fujian Cuisine) of this region. Min is the abbreviation and the ancient name of Fujian. And Min Cuisine, or called Fujian Cuisine, is one of the Top 8 Cuisines in China! Fujian Cuisine has much in common with the food and dishes in its nearby regions, like Taiwan and Guangdong. It is famous for its clean, clear, and fresh flavors, especially in its soups. Thanks to its unbeatable location of sitting along the coastline, its dishes are rich in a wide variety of seafood, like shrimp, snails, clams, sturgeon, oysters, and so on! The condiments mainly used include sugar, vinegar, satay, sauce, pepper, etc. Fuzhou and Xiamen are our picks of the best cities to savor Fujian Cuisine. Recommended Places to Eat in Fujian include the busy tourist streets like Zhongshan Road Pedestrian Street in Xiamen and Three Lanes and Seven Alleys in Fuzhou, as well as some little-known restaurants hidden at the corner of streets. If you ask much about the environment, you are also suggested to try some popular restaurants like Yanyu Restaurant (宴遇), Juchunyuan Restaurant (聚春园), Antai Restaurant (安泰楼酒家), etc. Food Price: from CNY 10 Food Flavor: clean, fresh, sweet, sour and slightly spicy Popular Dishes: Buddha Jumps over the Wall, Stewed Chicken with Three Cups Sauce, Tai Chi Prawns, Sweet and Sour Lychees, Drunk Chicken with Fermented Glutinous Rice, Steamed Strengthening Fish No.13 Visit Meizhou Island, the Birthplace of Chinese Goodness of the Sea - Mazu Meizhou Island (湄洲岛) enjoys the reputation of Mecca of the East. It is a wonderful place blessed with romantic and charming coastal scenery and rich in sacred Mazu Culture. There are as many as 13 golden beaches and five kilometers of magical maritime erosion rocks dotted along its coastline. The turquoise blue sea, bright sunshine, glittering beaches, and strange-shaped erosion rocks are eternal themes here. What a dreamland for vacation! Meizhou Island is also the birthplace of Mazu, Chinese Goddess of the Sea. Worship of Mazu spreads across the coastal provinces in China and centralized living places of overseas Chinese in Japan, Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, America, and so on. While there are over 5,000 Mazu Temples distributed in more than 20 countries and regions in the world, the Mazu Temple on Meizhou Island is the ancestor of all the rest. Every year, especially during the Mazu Festival held on lunar March 23, the birthday of Mazu, and September 9, the Ascension Day of Mazu, flocks of visitors will gather at Meizhou Island to worship Mazu. Type: Natural Island, Religious Temple Tickets: free for the island, CNY 30 per person for Mazu Temple Best Time to Visit: all year around Recommended Trip Length: one day or so Location: No.1588, Meizhou Avenue, Xiuyu District, Putian City, Fujian Province, China (福建省莆田市秀屿区湄洲大道1588号) No.14 Marvel at Charming Geological Wonders at Ningde Global Geopark Ningde Global Geopark (宁德世界地质公园) is located between the Taimu and Jiufeng Mountain ranges. The park is mostly famed for its splendid miarolitic mountainous land formations, gorgeous volcanic land formations, mysterious ravine and riverbed land formation, and coastal and marine erosion land formations that lead to a variety of wonderful mountains, caves, valleys, waterfalls, deep pools, and other beautiful attractions. On October 3, 2010, Ningde Geological Park was officially included in the UNESCO World Geological Park Network List and won the title of "Ningde Global Geopark"! The whole Ningde Global Geopark covers a large area of over 2,660 square kilometers. And it is composed of three main scenic areas, including Baishuiyang (白水洋), Baiyun Mountain (白云山), and Taimu Mountain (太姥山). The three areas are distributed in Ningde City, Fuan City, and Fuding City of Fujian Province, with at least 1.5 hours away by car between them. Normally, visitors ride a car from Fuzhou, the capital of this region, to visit Baishuiyang and Baiyun Mountain. Taimu Mountain is very close to Xiapu Mudflat. Driving from Xiapu to Taimu Mountain takes only one hour or so. There is also a bullet train station of the same name - Taimushan Railway Station, built about 17 kilometers and half an hour away from the scenic area by car. Taimushan Railway Station offers bullet train service to/from Xiamen, Fuzhou, Xiapu, Shanghai, Beijing, Hangzhou, Shenzhen, etc. Type: Natural Site, UNESCO World Geopark Tickets: from CNY 100 per person Best Time to Visit: all year around Recommended Trip Length: 1~2 days Location: Ningde City, Fujian (福建省宁德市) No.15 Explore Taining Scenic Tourist Area, Where China's Danxia Stories Begin Taining Danxia is a vital part of the Danxia Landscape in China, which was listed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2010. It is praised as "Where China's Danxia Stories Begin" by geoscientists from home and abroad. For visitors, when talking about Taining Danxia, it usually refers to Taining Scenic Tourist Area (泰宁风景区), which is composed of 9 scenic areas, including the most popular Dajin Lake Scenic Area (Big Golden Lake Scenic Area), Shangqing Stream, Taining Old Town, etc. Big Golden Lake Scenic Area (大金湖景区) offers splendid Danxia view, with uneven cliffs, high walls of rocks characterized by plunging crevasses, and rust-colored stone pillars rising from the water. There is also an exquisite temple built on the cliff, namely Ganlu Temple. The best way to explore this beautiful lake area is by boat, which will take the visitors winding through the narrow valleys and channels in between the rocks and cliffs. Shangqing Stream (上清溪) is the upper reach of Big Golden Lake. Its name, Shangqing, means fairyland in Taoism. And just as its name implies, Shangqing Stream is a beautiful wonderland. Visitors can enjoy bamboo rafting and learn distant and mysterious supernatural Taoist stories and fairytales here. Taining Old Town (泰宁古城) has a long history of over 1,340 years. Here, visitors can find ancient buildings built over 500 years, from the early Ming Dynasty to the late Qing Dynasty. Well-preserved Shangshudi Complex, the unique buildings of ancient ministers that are rare to see anywhere else, can also be found here. Type: Natural Site, World Natural Heritage Site, Danxia Mountain Tickets: from CNY 80 per person Best Time to Visit: all year around Recommended Trip Length: half day or one day Location: Taining County, Sanming City, Fujian, China (福建省三明市泰宁县) How to Plan a Fujian Tour Top Places to Visit in Fujian: Fujian Tulou, Gulangyu Island, Wuyi Mountain, Kaiyuan Temple, Sanfang Qixiang, South Putuo temple, Jimei School Village, Xiapu Mudflat, Meizhou Island, etc. Best Time to Visit Fujian: January ~ July & September ~ December for most places; March ~ November for Wuyi Mountain. How to Get to Fujian: Take flight to Xiamen Airport, Fuzhou Airport, Wuyishan Airport, or take high speed trains to Xiamen, Nanjing, Fuzhou, Wuyishan, Xiapu… Fujian is a pleasant destination to enjoy appealing coastal sightseeing, lay back in leisure and discover the culture and history of southeast China. You can spend about 2 days in most cities and destinations there to discover their top highlights. And usually 5-6 days is mostly planned to enjoy a Fujian province tour to have best fun in Xiamen, Fujian Tulou and Wuyishan! Among them, Xiamen and Fujian Tulou are the most classic and not-to-be missed for the first time to Fujian. Besides, if you want a deeper exploration in Fujian, Wuyi Mountain, Quanzhou, Fuzhou, and Xiapu Mudflat are the top recommendations! ☛ 5 Days Xiamen, Nanjing Tulou & Mount Wuyi Discovery Tour 1-2 days in Xiamen Xiamen is usually planned as the start of a Fujian tour where to enjoy pleasant and leisure time with the coastal landscape. Gulangyu Island, Nanputuo Temple, Huandao Road, etc. are the top highlights.. 1-2 days Fujian Tulou Many visitors enjoy a 1 day classic Fujian Tulou trip from Xiamen to visit Tianluokeng Tulou Cluster and other earthen buildings in Nanjing. Hongkeng Tulou Cluster and Chuxi Tulou Cluster in Yongding are great to add for a 2-day Tulou trip. Tulou in Hongkeng, Gaobei and Nanxi are also favored for an in-depth tour. 2-3 days in Wuyishan Most people spend 2 days at Wuyishan to visit Jiuqu Stream rafting, Tianyou Peak, Dahongpao Scenic Area, Wuyi Palace, impression Da Hong Pao, etc. Water Curtain Cave, Xiamei Village, etc. are great to add in another day. ☛ 7 Days Brilliant Fujian Tour ☛ 8 Days Bests of Fujian Tour (Xiamen, Tulou, Quanzhou, Wuyishan & Fuzhou) 1-2 days in Quanzhou If you want to learn about the famous Maritime Silk Road, consider a visit to Quanzhou, the UNESCO-recognized starting point of maritime trade globally during the Song-Yuan dynasties. There are nuermous historic relics waiting for your exploration. 4 Days Best Xiamen & Tulou Tour with Quanzhou UNESCO Heritages1-2 days in Fuzhou Fuzhou is another popular city to visit in Fujian. As the birthplace of Chinese naval and shipbuilding technology, it boasts a perfect blend of rich history, cultural depth, and natural beauty. 4 Days Classic Xiamen, Fuzhou & Fujian Tulou Tour2-3 days in Xiapu If you are interested in photography, plan at least 2 days to Xiapu to shoot the marvelous mudflat at Xiaohao, Beiqi, Dongbi, Shajiang and Yantian.
